Few years back, IELTS decided to walk with the trend and to become progressive with the current technology. This was first introduced in Australia and it is widely accepted across the world. Here the English remain same and the test carried out remains same. The only difference is the change from paper tests to computer tests. The Casper Academy of Excellence is a leading IELTS coaching centre in Kochi which helps you to get the best preparations for your IELTS training. The excellence in training with more than 20 years of experience had made Casper Academy highly popular.

What are the Difference between Computer Based IELTS and Paper Based IELTS?

Moving into the computer-based IELTS is surely a positive change. Here, all you need to know is that the test which was given using paper previously is now carried out through the computers. The listening module in the computer-based IELTS is a bit shorter of 10 minutes when compared to the paper-based IELTS. The skilled faculty at the Casper Academy will train you to attain a better band score in IELTS. Thus the Casper Academy is giving the best IELTS coaching in Ernakulam. Few other differences between computer-based and paper-based IELTS include:

Test Location

The computer-based test is actually new and improved. The rooms will be less crowded. Similarly, the seating here is more comfortable and the smaller room size means lesser number of candidates. In the case of paper IELTS, the rooms were large and could hold a higher capacity of candidates when compared to the computer-based IELTS.

Headphones Quality

In paper IELTS, most headphones are old and the quality has deteriorated. On the other hand, the computer-based IELTS is new and thus the gadgets are new and advanced. Moreover, most of the computer-based IELTS test centres provides noise cancellation headphones. This will help the candidates in easily concentrating on the recording and the rest of the test.

The Most Obvious – Paper and Computer

Each answer will be given on a piece of paper by pencil in paper-based IELTS. In the case of computer-based IELTS, the tests are conducted on the computer and the answers are recorded on the computer using a keyboard. This is the main difference between the two.

One module is shorter, one module is quicker and one module is easier

The listening module is shorter by 10 minutes, the speaking module is conducted on the same day to make it quicker and writing tests are easier as the word counts are shown on the screen.
